incidents.victim: Colorado water utilities (2 privately owned systems)
incidents.vector: Remote access to OT/SCADA equipment at two privately-owned water utilities, each serving fewer than 200 customers.
incidents.impact: Equipment was manipulated in both systems during August; no public safety impact or service disruption reported, but the incidents represent confirmed foreign OT compromise of US water infrastructure. Colorado Governor's office disclosed on Sept 19.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Identity Services Engine (enterprise and government globally)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated crafted request to an exposed Cisco ISE API endpoint bypasses authentication, granting root-level control with no user interaction required.
incidents.impact: Root access to Cisco ISE lets attackers modify network access policies, extract stored credentials, delete logs, and move laterally into every network segment ISE controls. CISA added CVE-2026-76460 (CVSS 10) to its KEV catalog on the same day Cisco disclosed and patched it.

incidents.victim: IT professionals and job seekers; 7,000+ cryptocurrency wallets; 30,000+ devices across 100 countries
incidents.vector: North Korean operators pose as AI/blockchain company recruiters on LinkedIn and freelance platforms, instructing applicants to download malware-laden files (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, StoatWaffle) during fake job interviews.
incidents.impact: More than $10.5 million stolen from 7,000+ cryptocurrency wallets; 30,000+ devices infected across 100 countries. Stolen identities used to infiltrate tech companies for follow-on intrusions. Japan disrupted first known laptop farm linked to the operation. FBI/DoD/Australia/Germany/Japan issued joint advisory.

incidents.victim: Open-source ecosystems (PyPI, npm, Docker Hub); AI/technology companies
incidents.vector: Trojanized MCP servers and malicious repository forks; DUSTMAKER credential-stealer hides in AI tool directories (.claude/, .vscode/, .cursor/), injects prompt-injection into codebases, and poisons CI/CD pipelines to steal OIDC tokens and sign malicious packages.
incidents.impact: Multiple large-scale supply chain compromises across PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub since March 2026; one victim's proprietary AI repository exfiltrated and held for ransom. Stolen credentials monetized through ransomware partnerships. Campaign uses AI automation to operate at scale.

incidents.victim: Organizations running ISSABEL PBX telephony management framework
incidents.vector: ISSABEL framework shipped with a hard-coded JWT signing key; attackers forge authentication tokens to bypass security and execute arbitrary code on connected Asterisk telephony servers with no credentials required.
incidents.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on PBX infrastructure confirmed in active exploitation by Shadowserver Foundation. Patch submitted but exploitation preceded public disclosure.

incidents.victim: Russian technology and defense companies (multiple, unspecified)
incidents.vector: Stolen VPN credentials used for initial access; GhostContainer backdoor installed on Microsoft Exchange servers via memory-injection technique; Active Directory exploited for privilege escalation and lateral movement to domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Multiple Russian defense and technology firms breached; attackers maintain persistent access, steal credentials, and impersonate legitimate users. Group previously targeted Chinese semiconductor, AI, and defense sectors and has now expanded operations to Russian companies.

incidents.victim: Revolut (London-based fintech, ~50 million customers)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized third-party access to Revolut systems exposed sensitive customer information; method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data of an unspecified number of customers exposed; a criminal group posted a public ultimatum demanding $3 million within 24 hours, threatening to sell the stolen data. Revolut reports no direct contact from attackers and is investigating.

incidents.victim: Travelers and enterprise users in hospitality networks globally
incidents.vector: Attackers manipulate DNS and HTTP traffic at hotel networks, redirecting travelers into device-code phishing via legitimate Microsoft sign-in pages or malware delivered as fake software updates (CaptiveCrunch campaign).
incidents.impact: Cloud identity compromise and endpoint malware installation on targeted travelers' devices; malware collects credentials, session tokens, security configurations, and remote-access history. Microsoft Threat Intelligence disclosed the active campaign.

incidents.victim: Enterprise organizations globally (sector unspecified)
incidents.vector: Attackers impersonate IT support over Microsoft Teams, persuade users to grant remote desktop access, then use PowerShell to deploy a malicious MSI package staging a portable Node.js C2 runtime.
incidents.impact: Persistent command-and-control established; attackers mapped Active Directory and attempted lateral movement to domain controllers and certificate authorities via WinRM. Each step uses legitimate enterprise tools, blending with normal operations to evade detection.

incidents.victim: Russia's Central Election Commission, Rostelecom, Vybory election platform
incidents.vector: Hackers breached election commission IT systems and contractor infrastructure, exfiltrating internal documents, server configurations, passwords, and developer communications.
incidents.impact: Internal documents, credentials, and communications from Russia's Central Election Commission and Rostelecom contractors stolen and shared with independent media days before Russia's State Duma parliamentary vote (Sep 18–20). Depth of access to voting or ballot-counting systems remains unclear.

incidents.victim: Government agencies in Guatemala, Honduras, Puerto Rico, Panama, Venezuela, Peru, Argentina
incidents.vector: Chinese espionage operators deployed the SparroWocky backdoor against government departments, exploiting Microsoft Exchange vulnerabilities to achieve persistent access; malware obfuscates analysis and leverages open-source code.
incidents.impact: Government agencies across seven Latin American countries breached; attackers can exfiltrate files, capture screenshots, and gather network intelligence. ESET assesses the campaign monitors regional governments' responses to US pressure on Chinese investments, including the Panama Canal ports dispute.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Secure Email Gateway
incidents.vector: Actively exploited zero-day (CVE-2026-76461) in Cisco Secure Email Gateway; specific vulnerability class not publicly detailed at time of disclosure.
incidents.impact: Second consecutive-day Cisco zero-day patched and confirmed exploited; attackers gained unauthorized access to email security appliances before patches were available. CISA added to KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: Dissidents, activists, and journalists in UK, US, Netherlands, and globally
incidents.vector: Iranian operators use WhatsApp and Telegram to impersonate trusted contacts or platform support, building rapport before delivering CHOSEN BRICK malware disguised as legitimate apps (Norton, Telegram, KeePass) or medical scan files.
incidents.impact: CHOSEN BRICK captures screen content, intercepts emails and messages, activates the microphone, and can wipe devices. Personal details of some victims published on pro-Iranian leak sites, increasing physical safety risks. NCSC/FBI/Netherlands AIVD issued joint advisory with indicators of compromise.

incidents.victim: Unnamed Spanish organization
incidents.vector: Attacker used a large language model as an autonomous agent to conduct reconnaissance, discover exposed credentials, identify an application vulnerability, and chain exploits to breach personal data stores.
incidents.impact: Personal data records were modified and corporate invoices accessed; Spain's AEPD data protection authority cited this as the first confirmed AI-agent-driven data breach, warning that AI-enabled attacks compress the defender's response window to near zero.

incidents.victim: IDScan (identity verification service); 153 million US and Canadian individuals
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised IDScan's identity verification platform and continuously exfiltrated driver's license records for over a year, ingesting nearly 400,000 new records per day.
incidents.impact: Approximately 153 million US and Canadian driver's licenses — roughly 63% of all US licenses — stolen and offered on the dark web; records include photos, addresses, and license numbers. US officials including a senior FBI official had records in the database. National security implications given adversary potential to link this data with other stolen identity databases.

incidents.victim: Americans targeted by Southeast Asia-based scam centers
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — cyber fraud (Chinese-language cybercrime platform)
incidents.vector: Chinese-language illicit marketplace connecting scam center operators with financial services, escrow, and money laundering facilitators; migrated to encrypted messaging app and cryptocurrency wallet under law enforcement pressure.
incidents.impact: Platform processed over $24 billion in digital assets since 2022 supporting cyber scam operations targeting Americans; reportedly used by North Korean hackers and multiple OFAC-designated entities. OFAC sanctioned the platform and two supporting entities; DOJ's Scam Center Strike Force seized infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Windows users and enterprises globally
incidents.vector: Two actively exploited Windows privilege escalation zero-days (CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880) addressed in September Patch Tuesday alongside CVE-2026-69829, a CVSS 9.8 Windows Shell RCE requiring no user interaction.
incidents.impact: Record 974 vulnerabilities patched in a single release, including 113 rated critical; two zero-days exploited before the patch dropped allow local privilege escalation to SYSTEM; DNS critical flaw CVE-2026-69730 affects Windows Server 2012 onward.

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (Germany)
incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering lured a city employee into solving a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA and pasting a malicious command; Rhysida ransomware was subsequently deployed across city networks.
incidents.impact: Rhysida ransomware encrypted Berlin city systems; attackers demanded $2 million, were refused, and publicly dumped stolen city data. ClickFix has now been observed enabling multiple nation-state and criminal ransomware deployments.

incidents.victim: 500+ French notary offices (approx. 7% of France's notaries)
incidents.vector: Phishing for initial access; attackers then silently modified client banking details within notary transaction systems over months or years to redirect wire transfers.
incidents.impact: Over €35 million stolen across 500+ firms during a four-year campaign; France's national cybersecurity agency (ANSSI) spent two years remediating; sector-wide procedural changes implemented to require out-of-band transaction confirmation.

incidents.victim: Two foreign-flagged commercial vessels bound for US ports
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the computer networks of two commercial vessels while in the Gulf of Mexico; attack method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: US Coast Guard and FBI conducted emergency boardings of both vessels (Aug 21 and Aug 24) after indications of network compromise; incidents part of a series of cyber attacks US officials have linked to Iran amid ongoing US-Iran tensions.
